thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: private-gpu-queue-depth for cust-zenith exceeded threshold in us-east-2 (queue 672, threshold 200). Autoscaler failing to add nodes, showing 'max node limit reached' and repeated node bootstrap timeouts. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/infr/metrics/cust-zenith

oncall-sam: seeing this. pulling logs now. first pass: autoscaler reports desired=12, max=8. queue_growth_rate ~ 20 reqs/s. customer reporting TTFB spikes.

maya: FYI I'm mid-deploy but can jump in 10. who is primary for customer comms?

oncall-sam: @support-ops please patch customer and set expectation: we're investigating, might redirect traffic.

support-ops: pinged customer rep (zenith-platform) — they confirm heavy batch jobs started at 10:12UTC. asking to pause non-urgent workloads.

leo: pasted autoscaler log snippet:
```
I1015 10:25:03 autoscaler.go:412] scale attempt failed: current=8 target=12 max=8
W1015 10:25:07 cloudprovider.go:233] launch instance timeout: image-pull-backoff
E1015 10:25:18 nodebootstrap.go:98] init script failed: unable to fetch userdata from s3://customer-artifacts/initrd.gz (i/o timeout)
```

nina: that userdata s3 path belongs to the customer's private registry endpoint. could be VPC endpoint problem.

eng-runtime: confirmed internal registry (s3 proxy) returned 504s starting 10:20UTC. networking traces show spike of packet loss on egress gateway for cust-zenith subnet.

oncall-sam: action list: 1) throttle non-critical traffic to cust-zenith (reduce rate to 30%); 2) enable temporary hosted-fallback routing for critical routes; 3) request override to bump max nodes for this customer while we investigate image pulls.

maya: I can open a quick firewall rule bypass to let bootstrap traffic reach public S3 for the node pool — needs infra approval. anyone have the runbook step id?

leo: runbook step: PROV-40. patch: 
```
# temporary: allow egress to s3.amazonaws.com from cust-zenith-subnet
aws ec2 create-network-acl-entry --network-acl-id acl-xxxx --rule-number 140 --egress --cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --port-range 443 --protocol tcp --rule-action allow
```

nina: be careful — cust-zenith requested private-only image sources earlier. we'll need customer ok for public egress.

support-ops: customer ok to allow egress for bootstrap (they just replied).

eng-runtime: I'm seeing node provision times ballooning: median 420s -> 1600s. pushing to infra to look at VM host capacity in us-east-2.

oncall-sam: I've filed infra ticket INC-17543 asking for temporary quota bump and imagehost bypass. linking here.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-17543 | gpu-pool-exhaustion-cust-zenith | Sev2 | https://incidents.redwood/INC-17543

leo: short-term mitigation applied: throttled batch jobs for cust-zenith via rate-limiter (policy zenith-batch set to 0.3). reduced inbound queue to ~180 over 6m. non-critical jobs queued at source.

maya: infra approved temporary node quota bump to 12 for cust-zenith while we confirm image pulls. applied. autoscaler attempted scale again - logs show nodes provisioned but stuck at 'NotReady' waiting on kubelet due to imagepull backoff.

nina: since imagepulls still failing, I pushed a lightweight interruption plan: mark older nodes as schedulable-only for latency-sensitive routes and cordon batch-heavy nodes. commands I ran:
```
kubectl get nodes -l pool=gpu-cust-zenith -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon
kubectl patch nodes <node> -p '{"spec": {"unschedulable": true}}'
```

eng-runtime: alternative: we can enable model-routing fallback to hosted-api for critical requests. config change: set route 'zenith-crit' -> hosted-us-east-2, TTL 30m. anyone want me to flip it?

oncall-sam: Flip it. we need to protect SLAs. do it and post exact toggle.

eng-runtime: flipped route. Verification: 98% of critical traffic now hits hosted endpoints. latency stabilized for critical flows. non-critical still queued at customer cluster.

support-ops: customer confirmed reduced user impact after fallback. thanks.

maya: infra found host-level disk pressure on several VM hosts which caused image server timeouts. infra moving some VMs and kickstarting image proxy. estimated recovery 20-30m.

leo: good. let's keep autoscaler disabled for 5m window to avoid thrash once nodes recover (autoscaler set to pause).

oncall-sam: summary for handoff to night: - cause: image proxy + host disk pressure -> node bootstrap timeouts -> autoscaler hitting maxNodes -> queue growth. - mitigation: throttle batch jobs (policy applied), enabled hosted fallback for critical routes, temporary node quota bump, infra migrating VMs and fixing image proxy. - open items: verify full node readiness across new nodes, re-enable autoscaler after steady state, review customer's private registry VPC endpoint, consider adding local registry cache for cust-zenith.

nina: leaving instructions in INC-17543: verify kubelet logs on recovered nodes: `journalctl -u kubelet | grep image` and check for 'Pull complete' events.

eng-runtime: posting quick snippet to re-enable autoscaler (after go-ahead):
```
# set autoscaler back to default behavior
kubectl annotate deployment cluster-autoscaler autoscaler.paused-til-  \
  --overwrite=false || true
# or /api/autoscale/unpause?cust=zenith
```

oncall-sam: handing off to @maya for night coverage. please follow these steps if queue > 250 again: 1) reapply throttle, 2) flip fallback routing, 3) contact infra pager, 4) escalate to Eng Runtime if image pulls persist.

maya: acknowledged. I'll follow up with a postmortem draft tomorrow AM. leaving channel; ping me if anything breaks. :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Incident INC-17543 status: mitigated -> monitoring. assigned to: maya, eng-runtime, infra.

support-ops: customer rep will schedule a runbook review tomorrow to discuss adding a local image cache. they also asked for a timeline for permanent quota increase — we'll coordinate with sales.

oncall-sam: thanks everyone. closing active paging loop.
